title: Redundant Wrapper Layer (Anemic Delegation)
pattern: Creating adjacent layers of abstraction where intermediate layers do nothing but delegate to the next lower layer without transforming data, adding validation, or checking security.
why_bad: It adds structural bloat, slows down compilation, and increases the surface area of code that must be maintained, without providing any decoupling or abstraction benefit.
detection: A class or method in a multi-tier architecture whose implementation is a single-line call to a matching method in the adjacent lower layer.
counterexample: Explicitly separated interfaces at physical deployment boundaries (like RPC gateways) where delegation is necessary for network dispatching.
fix: Collapse the redundant layer, letting callers invoke the underlying service directly.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Middle Man"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 7.
